newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu says "no thanks" to salary rise.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu says "no thanks" to salary rise.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Wednesday he wants to forgo a mandated salary rise while his government is trying to tighten its belt.

Netanyahu's spokesman said the prime minister told his cabinet during an economic debate that he would ask parliament's finance committee to stop a 6.9 percent cost of living increment from being added to his monthly salary of 20,320 shekels ($6,250).
The committee on Monday approved the rise for all 120 members of the parliament, in which Netanyahu holds a Likud party seat.
In the last year, legislators' salaries have risen by 33 percent in compensation for income lost when new regulations banned them from non-parliamentary work.

"At this time of budget cuts and our attempt to get the economy on the right growth track, it is only fitting that elected officials serve as an example to other citizens," the spokesman quoted Netanyahu as saying.
"Therefore, I will request to forgo the addition to my salary," he said.
Israel's 1997 budget of approximately 190 billion shekels ($58.5 billion) includes some seven billion shekels in spending cuts, new taxes and other revenue measures.
Finance Minister Dan Meridor, an architect of the budget package, called on other members of parliament to turn down the raises.
"I am trying to persuade them and I hope I succeed," he told Israel Radio. ($1=3.25 shekels)
